title: Resolve remaining production-scope native-only blocking findings gating the production-closure candidate pin
summary: Worker-side fixes removed the code-fixable findings (nvml telemetry load, onnxruntime presence probe, System.Management nuget). Remaining production-scope blockers are architecture-authority decisions: the Npgsql PostgreSQL adapter (authority re-confirmed 2026-10-02) and eight third-party Rust crates in xstore/xcorpus. A governed sanction or migration contract is required before the §3 native-only prerequisite can pass.
origin: Production-closure directive §3 prerequisite derivation (--production-prereqs) against release-gate report gate-20261002-120127.json; per-finding production/dev scope split inspected

problem.summary: release-gate step native-dependency = FAIL on production-scope blocking findings. Remaining after worker fixes: Npgsql (postgresql_required + third_party_nuget) and 8 cargo crates (third_party_rust_crates). Both require governor adjudication — removal conflicts with the live authority model.

open_decisions.finding: postgresql_required + third_party_nuget: Npgsql PackageReference in GPTBridge.XingchengLearning.csproj and Npgsql source-ref in Pg.cs (scope=production, blocking=true)
open_decisions.context: 2026-10-02 decision reversal kept PostgreSQL (gptbridge_xingcheng*) as the formal structured metadata authority and cancelled the xstore metadata takeover. Directive §143 lists PostgreSQL required = false as a production end-state, which conflicts with the current authority assignment.
options: A. Sanction Npgsql as the governed metadata adapter for the production-closure phase; record §143 as a deferred end-state with an explicit transition contract
B. Declare a bounded migration contract moving the xingcheng metadata plane off PostgreSQL before certification proceeds
C. Split scopes: sanction Npgsql for the learning/orchestration plane while the production runtime binary carries no PostgreSQL dependency

open_decisions.finding: third_party_rust_crates blocking=8: xstore/Cargo.toml (serde_json, sha2, memmap2, unicode_categories, time), xcorpus/Cargo.toml (serde_json, sha2, unicode-normalization)
open_decisions.context: These implement content hashing (sha2), JSON contracts (serde_json), memory-mapping (memmap2) and Unicode semantics. In-repo reimplementation is error-prone and worse for auditability than a governed allowlist.
options: A. Publish a governed sanctioned-crate allowlist for the Rust plane naming these crates+versions
B. Mandate in-repo reimplementation (high risk, multi-week)
C. Mixed: sanction hash/serialization crates, audit or replace the rest

open_decisions.finding: The scan treats any production-scope source reference to a forbidden module as blocking, including load-and-release presence probes
open_decisions.context: The removed onnxruntime EP probe and nvml telemetry were detection/telemetry surfaces, not dependency use. If a probe-sanctioned class is wanted (detect presence without linking), the check vocabulary needs a governed addition; otherwise the removals performed stand as the contract.
options: A. Keep strict reading (removal was correct; no sanction needed)
B. Introduce a governed detection-probe classification for named vendor DLLs
